message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (replace <ZONE> with your preferred zone)
ZONENAME=<ZONE>

# 2. Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --zone=$ZONENAME \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM allocation. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` + `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk. |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD (`pd-balanced`) vs HDD (`pd-standard`). |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keeps the VM running during host maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional shell script that runs at first boot (e.g., install drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, just change the values accordingly.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw REST endpoint, here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/<ZONE>/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": "100",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to call it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your actual project ID and zone. Save the JSON above to `instance.json`.

---

## 🎯 Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project**: Ensure you have billing enabled and the Compute Engine API activated.  
- [ ] **Zone**: Pick a zone that supports the RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-b`, `us-east1-c`).  
- [ ] **GPU quota**: Verify you have enough GPU quota for the selected zone.  
- [ ] **Firewall**: Add firewall rules if you need inbound traffic (the tags above open ports 80/443).  

Once the instance is created, SSH into it and run:

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install nvidia-driver-535 -y   # installs the driver that supports RTX A6000
```

Now you’re ready to start training or rendering workloads on the RTX A6000!
